description: Increasing compound climate hazards affect housing health infrastructure energy and migration.
Fiscal capacity may enable resilience investment or constrain adaptation under austerity.
Water stress biodiversity loss food production and land-use conflict may create cascading regional risks.
Trust may recover fragment or collapse depending on accountability performance and public voice.
Energy burden and grid stress interact with climate exposure electrification and public trust.
Conflict sanctions trade fragmentation and supply-chain disruptions may reshape strategic options.
AI deployment may outpace audit appeal rights procurement standards and institutional oversight.
Care labor capacity affects public health aging resilience and household vulnerability.
Deferred maintenance creates hidden fragility across public systems and long-lived assets.
Learning systems may or may not build the civic and anticipatory capacity needed for uncertainty.
